_about: Body Scout. `official` (sourced, one link per number) and `research` (judgement calls with their why and evidence) are written by hand. `reach`, `segments`, `build`, `movement`, `flexibility` and `game` are derived from them by datasets/players/tools/build_bodies.py: do not edit those by hand, change `research` and run the tool. A block marked "estimate": true is an estimate in every number, by the method it states. Method and references: datasets/players/BODY_SOURCES.md.
name: Carlos Alcaraz

official.how: The ATP Tour profile's own data (HeightCm, WeightKg, BirthDate, PlayHand, BackHand), read from the JSON the profile page loads.

armSpanRatio.why: style.json: a compact build (video notes), so slightly under the 1.03 norm; not measured
armSpanRatio.searched: No published wingspan found (searched Nov 11, 2026; only unsourced fan-site guesses).

legShift.why: standard leg share: no evidence of an unusually long- or short-legged build

build.massSits: legs: thick thighs and strong calves under a compact trunk
build.look: style.json (video): 'compact and powerful, thick thighs'; appearance.json: long hair, hairband, beard, black sleeve on the racket forearm
build.mulWhy: style.json build note 'thick thighs' (US Open clips)

movement.why: Named by Fils among the quickest ('Carlos is fast'; over 40 m he would take himself, Carlos or de Minaur); style.json: 'explosive crossover into a huge first stride'.
movement.slides: Low lunging slides on the outside leg, hard courts included (style.json: 'plants low on the outside leg and hits from the lunge; bends right down to dig out low balls on the run').

evidence.claim: Arthur Fils, asked for the quickest men on tour (Tennis Channel, Indian Wells 2026), named Davidovich Fokina, Mpetshi Perricard, himself, Shelton, Monfils, Alcaraz and de Minaur: 'I think 40m I'd take myself, or Carlos, or Demon.'
running/firstStep: 'explosive crossover into a huge first stride; back leg fully stretched behind'

flexibility.why: style.json (video): plants low on the outside leg and bends right down on the run; a little above the tour norm, not measured
flexibility.spreadWhy: Wider than typical: the low lunge in his US Open clips (style.json running/braking).

evidence.claim: running/braking: 'plants low on the outside leg and hits from the lunge; bends right down to dig out low balls on the run (v1 129.0)'

reach.method: no published wingspan found: arm span = 1.020 x height. style.json: a compact build (video notes), so slightly under the 1.03 norm; not measured
reach.standingReachHow: flat-footed, fingertips overhead: shoulder height + arm + 3% of height for the raised shoulder girdle (estimate)
reach.racketReachHow: body centre line to the racket's sweet spot, arm straight out at shoulder height, no lean or step: half the shoulder-joint spacing + upper arm + forearm + 0.50 m (wrist to sweet spot of a 68.6 cm racket). Estimate.
reach.overheadRacketReachHow: sweet spot height with the arm straight up, feet flat (a serve adds the jump). Estimate.

segments.method: standard ratios x his sourced height (Drillis & Contini via Winter; widths as in BODY_SOURCES.md), moved only by research.legShift, research.armSpanRatio and research.build.mul. Not measured on him.

check.what: head+neck + trunk + thigh + shin + foot height must equal his height (within 1 cm); shoulder-joint spacing + 2 x (upper arm + forearm + hand) must equal his arm span

build.bmiHow: weight / height^2 from the official numbers
build.typeHow: from BMI: under 21.8 lean, 21.8-24.2 athletic, above powerful (men's Olympic tennis mean 23.25)
build.massSits: legs: thick thighs and strong calves under a compact trunk
build.look: style.json (video): 'compact and powerful, thick thighs'; appearance.json: long hair, hairband, beard, black sleeve on the racket forearm

proportions.method: fractions of his height, seen from the front. Widths: Drillis & Contini outer widths; thickness baselines are estimates for an average tour build, scaled by sqrt(BMI / 23.25) and by research.build.mul (the features the Appearance Scout and the video notes call out).

movement.method: no per-player tracking speeds are published for most of the tour, so: the game's own body formula (top = 6.6 x sqrt(h) / w^0.25, accel = 8.6 / w / sqrt(h), h = height / 1.85, w = weight / 75; its 6.6 m/s matches the ATP's 23.58 km/h maximum speed for men's tennis) x a small rating from the evidence below x age (after 30: -0.6% top speed and -0.8% first step per year; legends are modelled at their prime).

ratings.why: Named by Fils among the quickest ('Carlos is fast'; over 40 m he would take himself, Carlos or de Minaur); style.json: 'explosive crossover into a huge first stride'.

movement.changeOfDirectionHow: 1 = average tour player: sqrt(80.8 kg / his weight) x rating x age (a lighter body stops and restarts faster)
movement.slides: Low lunging slides on the outside leg, hard courts included (style.json: 'plants low on the outside leg and hits from the lunge; bends right down to dig out low balls on the run').

evidence.claim: Arthur Fils, asked for the quickest men on tour (Tennis Channel, Indian Wells 2026), named Davidovich Fokina, Mpetshi Perricard, himself, Shelton, Monfils, Alcaraz and de Minaur: 'I think 40m I'd take myself, or Carlos, or Demon.'
running/firstStep: 'explosive crossover into a huge first stride; back leg fully stretched behind'

flexibility.method: normal active ranges (AAOS, from the Biomechanics Coach's datasets/anatomy/joints.json), changed per player only with evidence; nobody on the roster has published goniometer numbers.
flexibility.flexWhy: style.json (video): plants low on the outside leg and bends right down on the run; a little above the tour norm, not measured

hip_abduction.source: estimate: normal range x his flex 1.06 (style.json (video): plants low on the outside leg and bends right down on the run; a little above the tour norm, not measured)

hip_internal_rotation.source: estimate: normal range x his flex 1.06 (style.json (video): plants low on the outside leg and bends right down on the run; a little above the tour norm, not measured)

shoulder_external_rotation.source: typical elite range (playing shoulder of tour players: about +10 external, -10 internal rotation; Ellenbecker)

shoulder_internal_rotation.source: typical elite range (playing shoulder of tour players: about +10 external, -10 internal rotation; Ellenbecker)

widestStance.spreadHow: angle between the legs in his widest slide or stretch (110 = typical tour player, 180 = full split). Wider than typical: the low lunge in his US Open clips (style.json running/braking).

evidence.claim: running/braking: 'plants low on the outside leg and hits from the lunge; bends right down to dig out low balls on the run (v1 129.0)'

why.armSpanM: estimate: 1.020 x height, style.json: a compact build (video notes), so slightly under the 1.03 norm; not measured
why.legLengthM: hip joint to floor: (0.530) x height (Drillis & Contini)
why.shoulderW: bone width acromion to acromion: 0.235 x height
why.hipW: outer hip width: 0.191 x height, scaled by build
why.shoulderJointW: shoulder joint centres: shoulderW minus ~3 cm a side (for the skeleton)
why.hipJointW: hip joint centres: 0.095 x height (for the skeleton: the legs hang from here, not from the hip's outer edge)
why.reachM: body centre to sweet spot, arm straight out, standing still; a lean or a step adds to it
why.overheadReachM: sweet spot height with the arm straight up, feet flat (serve contact before the jump)
why.topSpeed: m/s, estimate: body formula x mover 1.06 x age 1.000. Named by Fils among the quickest ('Carlos is fast'; over 40 m he would take himself, Carlos or de Minaur); style.json: 'explosive crossover into a huge first stride'.
why.accel: m/s^2, estimate: body formula x first step 1.10 x age 1.000
why.cod: 1 = average: sqrt(80.8 / weight) x 1.12 x age 1.000
why.flex: style.json (video): plants low on the outside leg and bends right down on the run; a little above the tour norm, not measured
why.splitDepth: share of his leg length the hips drop in his widest stance: 1 - cos(130 deg / 2)
